email.definition: A message sent electronically through the internet to another person or group.

report.definition: The act of informing by verbal report.

proposal.definition: The act of making a proposal.

invoice.definition: An itemized statement of money owed for goods shipped or services rendered.

contract.definition: (contract bridge) the highest bid becomes the contract setting the number of tricks that the bidder must make.

letter.definition: A written message addressed to a person or organization.

newsletter.definition: Report or open letter giving informal or confidential news of interest to a special group.

press-release.definition: An official statement sent to journalists to announce news or an event.

deadline.definition: The latest time by which something must be finished.

milestone.definition: Stone post at side of a road to show distances.

deliverable.definition: Something that can be provided as the product of development.

stakeholder.definition: Someone entrusted to hold the stakes for two or more persons betting against one another.

benchmark.definition: A standard by which something can be measured or judged.

kpi.definition: A key performance indicator, meaning a measurable value used to track progress toward an important business or organizational objective.
kpi.exampleUsage: The team chose response time as one KPI.

roi.definition: (corporate finance) the amount, expressed as a percentage, that is earned on a company's total capital calculated by dividing the total capital into earnings before interest, taxes, or dividends are paid.

strategy.definition: An elaborate and systematic plan of action.

objective.definition: Undistorted by emotion or personal bias.

teamwork.definition: Cooperative work done by a team (especially when it is effective).

brainstorm.definition: The clear (and often sudden) understanding of a complex situation.

feedback.definition: The process in which part of the output of a system is returned to its input in order to regulate its further output.

review.definition: An article that evaluates a book, film, product, or event.

delegation.definition: A group of representatives or delegates.

coordination.definition: The skillful and effective interaction of movements.

synergy.definition: The working together of two things (muscles or drugs for example) to produce an effect greater than the sum of their individual effects.

consensus.definition: Agreement in the judgment or opinion reached by a group as a whole.

alignment.definition: An organization of people (or countries) involved in a pact or treaty.

follow-up.definition: A later action, message, or meeting used to continue, check, or complete something discussed earlier.
follow-up.exampleUsage: She sent a follow-up email after the meeting.

touch-base.definition: Contact someone briefly to exchange information or discuss what happens next.

circle-back.definition: A planned return to a subject or problem for further discussion.

moving-forward.definition: A business expression meaning from this point onward or in future work.
moving-forward.exampleUsage: Moving forward, the team will use the updated schedule.

action-items.definition: Specific tasks that people agree to complete after a meeting or discussion.
action-items.exampleUsage: The meeting notes list three action items.

best-practice.definition: An educational approach widely judged to be the most effective way to help learners achieve a specific goal.

takeaway.definition: Prepared food that is intended to be eaten off of the premises.

bottleneck.definition: To become narrow, like a bottleneck.
